item.title: The US military’s race to make fake blood
item.description:
Source: MIT Technology Review
The US military’s urgent need for synthetic blood solutions is driven by a critical shortage of blood in both military and civilian contexts, which contributes to preventable deaths. A 2007 incident involving a helicopter on a 'blood run' to transport blood to a field hospital in Iraq underscores the life-or-death stakes of timely transfusions. Lieutenant Commander Robert Murray, a Navy officer and DARPA program manager, highlights that 90% of preventable battlefield deaths result from hemorrhage, with 1% of 1.2 million trauma patients in the US receiving blood before hospital arrival. Globally, this shortage leads to millions of preventable deaths annually. Blood’s storage limitations—whole blood lasts 35 days refrigerated, platelets only weeks, and red blood cells or plasma days—create logistical challenges. Murray leads DARPA’s $73 million RAPIID program, aiming to develop shelf-stable plasma, platelets, and red blood cells. This builds on prior efforts like FSHARP, which showed promise in animal trials. RAPIID seeks to deploy synthetic blood components by 2029, addressing the 36-minute window critical for survival after injury. Plasma, the most advanced component, has been freeze-dried since the 1930s but faced hepatitis risks in the 1960s. Recent FDA approvals allow its emergency use by the military and civilians. Platelet preservation remains difficult, with Cellphire’s freeze-dried human platelets showing promise but limited scalability. Red blood cells face hurdles in mimicking hemoglobin’s oxygen-carrying function without immunological complications, as seen in failed HBOC trials like HemAssist, which caused severe side effects. Lab-grown blood via 'blood pharming' using stem cells faces cost and storage issues, with DARPA’s 2008 initiative abandoned due to high costs. Murray emphasizes the complexity of solving these challenges, noting that while individual projects may succeed, integrating them into practical solutions remains uncertain. The urgency is heightened by scenarios like Okinawa’s blood supply vulnerability, where a missile strike could disrupt critical infrastructure. Murray’s work reflects a broader push to overcome blood shortages, balancing technological innovation with the immediate need to save lives in combat and civilian emergencies.

item.title: The facts matter: Google updates AI Overviews, drawing more attention to linked sources
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Google is rolling out updates to its Search AI features, including AI Mode and AI Overviews, to enhance user confidence and improve source visibility. The updates aim to make inline source links more prominent in search results, appearing higher in responses more frequently. Users will now see more engaging links with thumbnail photos and a more click-encouraging design, particularly when exploring topics in-depth via AI Mode. Additionally, Google is testing a new section at the top of some responses labeled 'Quick results from the web,' which will highlight the best sources for a search with brief explanations. For timely news, the company is introducing a 'prominent carousel' of articles in Search, allowing users to quickly browse recent or breaking news stories. The 'Preferred Sources' feature is also being updated to help users find content from favored websites more easily. In video results, Google has added clickable creator and publisher profiles, directing users to their Search Profiles. These profiles will aggregate articles, social media posts, and videos, with a 'Follow on Google' button in the knowledge panel for the Discover feed. The updates are being rolled out throughout October, with users encouraged to monitor for changes. The changes address previous shortcomings in source visibility and usability, aiming to provide clearer, more trustworthy information through improved design and organization of search results.

item.title: Microsoft says it made Windows 11 zippier, especially on PCs with less RAM
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Microsoft has released updates for Windows 11 aimed at improving performance, particularly on devices with limited RAM. The company claims the operating system is up to 20% more responsive, achieved through enhanced memory efficiency and management. A key change allows Windows 11 to retain up to 2GB more of active data in memory, reducing reliance on slower storage and maintaining responsiveness when opening multiple apps or browser tabs. Navjot Virk, Microsoft’s corporate vice president of Windows Experiences, highlighted that PCs with 8GB of RAM may see "an especially meaningful difference," noting the growing cost of upgrading RAM due to AI data centers demanding high memory capacity. For systems with 8GB or less, Windows 11 will now load widgets only when users open them, freeing over 200MB of memory for other tasks. Additional improvements include faster pairing of AirPods with PCs and enhanced Bluetooth headphone reliability. Windows Hello logins are also described as easier, faster, and more reliable. Windows Insider testers can preview an AI-powered Search feature, which Microsoft is transforming into a chatbot interface, enabling thousands of actions through voice or text commands. The revamped Photos app includes a redesigned gallery that aggregates images from local storage, OneDrive, and iCloud, with the built-in editor loading 25% faster and the native viewer 30% quicker. These updates are now available to Windows Insiders, with Microsoft emphasizing ongoing refinements based on user feedback.

item.title: Your expensive drill feels useless because you're using the wrong bit
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek
Using the wrong drill bit can render an expensive drill ineffective, even if the tool itself is capable. The issue often stems from a mismatch between the bit and the screw's head type or size, leading to stripped screws and damaged tools. Drill bits and driver bits serve different purposes: drill bits create holes, while driver bits grip screw heads to turn them. A loose fit between the bit and the screw recess reduces contact area, causing wobble and cam-out, where the bit slips out of the screw head during driving. Common screw head types include Phillips (with tapered walls), Pozidriv (parallel walls and secondary ribs), Robertson (square socket), Torx (six-lobe star shape), and Allen (hexagonal). Each has specific size standards, such as Phillips PH1-PH3 or Torx T10-T40. Using a bit one size too small, like a PH1 in a PH2 recess, results in minimal contact and increased cam-out risk. Before driving, users should test bits by hand, ensuring they fit snugly without play and fully engage the screw. Proper alignment is critical; even slight misalignment shifts force unevenly, triggering cam-out. Adjusting the drill's clutch to kick out before the screw strips prevents damage. A pilot hole is also essential to prevent wood splitting and ease bit engagement, with depths varying by wood type: 70% of the screw's diameter in softwoods and closer to 90% in hardwoods. Bit material and wear further impact performance. Standard bits are made from chrome vanadium or S2 steel, hardened to 58-62 HRC, while impact-rated bits use softer steel (55-58 HRC) with a torsion zone to absorb shocks. Worn bits with rounded or chipped edges mimic undersized bits, exacerbating stripping issues. While factors like torque settings or screw quality matter, they typically worsen existing fit problems rather than being the primary cause. Correct bit selection and maintenance are vital to ensure a drill functions as intended, avoiding costly repairs and material waste.

item.title: Which Sling TV Plan Carries the Channels You Watch?
item.description:
Source: PCMag
Sling TV offers modular streaming plans tailored to specific channel preferences, with no contract required. The choice of plan depends on the channels a user watches, as Sling does not provide a single bundled package. Sling Orange focuses on sports and family programming, including ESPN, Disney, and AMC, while Sling Blue emphasizes news and entertainment with Fox News, MS NOW, FX, and Bravo. Sports channels like FS1 and NFL Network are available on Sling Blue and Sling Select. Combination packages, such as Sling Orange & Blue or Essentials & Select, merge channels from both plans. Plans start at $19.99 monthly for Sling Essentials and Sling Select, with options to add Sports Extra for $11–$15 monthly to access additional sports networks like ACC, SEC, and Big Ten. Local ABC, FOX, and NBC stations are available on Sling Blue, Select, and combination plans in select markets, though CBS is not included on any plan. Users can also opt for add-ons like Entertainment Extra or the 4 Extras Deal for $13 monthly, though Sports Extra is excluded from the latter. Sling’s month-to-month model allows cancellation or pauses without fees, and a free trial (Sling Freestream) offers 600+ live channels without a credit card. DVR storage of 50 hours is included, with an optional $5 monthly upgrade for unlimited DVR. Stream limits vary by plan: 1 stream for Orange/Essentials, 3 for Blue/Select, and 4 for combination packages. For niche channels not covered by base plans, Sling provides seven add-on packages. Users should check their zip code for local channel availability, as some plans exclude CBS. The article advises verifying market-specific access and pairing Sling with an over-the-air antenna for local networks like FOX if needed.

item.title: How much more can nuclear power plants give?
item.description:
Source: MIT Technology Review
In response to rising electricity demand driven by AI and data centers, nuclear power plants in the U.S. are undergoing upgrades to increase their output. Constellation, the nation’s largest nuclear operator, announced plans to add nearly a gigawatt of capacity across 11 reactors at six plants, requiring over $4.3 billion in investments. The Department of Energy recently approved a $4.2 billion loan for Vistra to upgrade three plants, while another $4 billion in federal funding will support upgrades at Vistra’s facilities in Pennsylvania and Ohio. These projects aim to add 433 megawatts of capacity, with Meta already committing to long-term electricity purchases. Similar deals include Google’s 20-year agreement with Constellation, which helped justify the costly uprates. Power uprates involve replacing equipment and using more highly enriched fuel to boost reactor output by up to 20%, with recent examples including a $475 million project at Alabama’s Browns Ferry plant that increased capacity by 14%. Between 2001 and 2010, the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission approved 80 uprates, compared to 33 between 2011 and 2020. While uprates are less expensive than building new reactors, they remain costlier than solar farms or natural-gas plants. The U.S. nuclear fleet currently provides 98 gigawatts of capacity, with 2.4 gigawatts of potential uprates approved through 2032. However, grid operator PJM projects a 30-gigawatt increase in peak demand by 2030 due to AI, highlighting that even maximum uprate potential would only address a fraction of future needs. Despite this, leveraging existing reactors remains a critical short-term strategy for expanding zero-emissions power, though long-term growth will likely require new reactor construction.

item.title: USAF will upgrade F-16s ' computers to keep venerable Falcon fighters flying until the 2040s — popular 4th generation aircraft will have flown almost seven decades by the time they retire
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News
The US Air Force is seeking a Next-Generation Mission Compute (NGMC) system to replace the outdated Modular Mission Computer in its F-16 Block 40/42/50/52 jets, which are central to the service's Viper fleet. The upgrade aims to extend the F-16's service life until the 2040s, nearly seven decades after its 1974 debut. The NGMC initiative, announced in September 2026, calls for open, swappable hardware that separates flight-safety and mission computing functions, with space for GPUs and AI capabilities. The Air Force emphasized a modular, software-defined design aligned with the Modular Open Systems Approach and Sensor Open Systems Architecture (SOSA) standards, aiming to break vendor lock and allow future upgrades from multiple suppliers. The new system must fit existing hardware constraints, rehost legacy software (the Operational Flight Program), and accommodate growing computational demands from new sensors. While the upgrade is still in the exploratory phase without a formal request for proposals, the project faces significant challenges, including reworking six million lines of legacy code and ensuring reliability amid increasing complexity. The F-16's extended service timeline was reaffirmed in 2023, with plans to keep up to 300 jets operational until 2048. However, the upgrade's success hinges on overcoming technical hurdles and securing funding, as the aircraft remains critical to both US and allied air forces despite the lack of a modern replacement. The Air Force's 2016 Raytheon upgrade, which promised enhanced processing power but faced delays, highlights the ongoing struggle to modernize the aging platform. With over 2,100 F-16s still active globally and nearly half of the US Air Force's fighter inventory comprising these jets, the NGMC initiative underscores the Viper's enduring role in military operations.

item.title: KDE turns 30 with Plasma 6.8, remote upgrades, and an X11 farewell
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica
KDE celebrated its 30th anniversary on October 14 with the release of Plasma 6.8, dubbed the '30th Anniversary Edition,' which marks the project's transition to Wayland and the retirement of native X11 session support. The update prepares Plasma for future developments while ensuring legacy X11 applications continue to function via XWayland compatibility. Users on Plasma 6.7 will retain their existing X11 sessions, though Plasma will no longer support starting new X11 sessions. This shift aligns with GNOME’s decision to drop X11 by default in 2025, ending a 42-year legacy of the X11 protocol. Plasma 6.8 introduces several enhancements, including expanded support for window decorations like shadows and rounded corners in third-party apps, a streamlined Union theming system, and default Nvidia triple buffering. New tools such as Kup backup integration and kscreenctl—a command-line utility for adjusting display configurations—expand customization options. The updated System Monitor allows users to pin processes to specific CPU cores via the GUI. Remote desktop users benefit from a revamped Plasma server with features like clipboard synchronization between client and server, 'Exclusive Mode' for virtual displays, and adaptive streaming for slower networks. Linux enthusiasts can watch 'The KDE Documentary — A Story of Free Software Underdogs,' a new film showcasing the project’s history, including a humorous opening montage of contributors struggling to define KDE. The release underscores KDE’s evolution while embracing modern display protocols and user-centric improvements.

item.title: CFTC Draws a Federal-State Line for Prediction Markets
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has proposed two measures to clarify the regulatory status of prediction-market contracts, drawing a federal-state line over jurisdiction. The first measure expands the definition of a swap to include contracts tied to cultural events, weather, politics, and sports, asserting these are commonly treated as swaps in trading markets and aim to resolve legal uncertainty. The second measure is an interim final rule excluding casino-style gambling, such as sportsbook wagers and casino games, from the swap definition, effective upon publication in the Federal Register. Both proposals include 30-day comment periods and were submitted to the White House Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs on September 28 before being released on October 9. The CFTC argues event contracts fall under federal derivatives rules under the Commodity Exchange Act, while states claim prediction markets are subject to state gambling laws. This jurisdictional conflict is already in court, with the Third and Ninth Circuit Courts of Appeals split on whether event contracts qualify as federally regulated swaps. New Jersey has petitioned the Supreme Court to review a case involving Kalshi, with 39 states and the District of Columbia joining the NFL in urging the court to take up the dispute. The NFL supports New Jersey’s petition, warning that without Supreme Court clarity, operators could exploit regulatory gaps, risking consumer protection and sports integrity. The CFTC’s proposals do not resolve whether states can enforce gambling laws on federally regulated exchanges, leaving the broader federal-state regulatory battle unresolved. The next steps involve closing the 30-day comment periods, with the CFTC considering revisions or finalizing the rules. Separately, the Supreme Court must decide whether to hear New Jersey’s petition, while the CFTC seeks to formalize its interpretation of event contracts before court rulings provide further guidance. The measures establish a regulatory boundary between event contracts classified as swaps and conventional gambling products, influencing how prediction-market operators structure offerings and defend against state enforcement, but do not settle the courts’ question of federal and state law interaction. The dispute highlights the ongoing conflict over how to regulate prediction markets, with states and the CFTC each advocating for exclusive oversight.

item.title: Google's $5 AI plan is getting a major downgrade starting November 13
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Google is significantly altering its AI subscription plans, starting November 13, 2026, by restricting access to Gemini's Pro models for users on the $5 Google AI Plus plan. Current subscribers will no longer be able to manually select Pro models in the Gemini app or AI Mode in Google Search after this date. Instead, continued access to Pro models will require upgrading to the more expensive Google AI Pro subscription, which costs $20 per month in the U.S.—four times the previous price. The change was first noted by a Reddit user via Droid-Life, who reported that Google has begun sending emails to AI Plus subscribers informing them of the upcoming shift. While users on the cheaper plan will still have access to Gemini's Flash models, those relying on Pro models for complex tasks, reasoning, or research will need to pay the higher fee. Google AI Pro also includes additional perks such as YouTube Premium Lite, Google Home Premium, Google Health Premium, and 5TB of shared cloud storage across Google services. These added benefits aim to justify the increased cost, though the move effectively doubles the price for Pro model access. The company emphasizes that AI Plus subscribers will retain Flash model access, but the restriction on Pro models marks a notable shift in Google's strategy to monetize advanced AI capabilities. The change affects both the Gemini app and Google Search, with users needing to adjust their subscriptions to maintain access to the more powerful Pro models.

item.title: Six wild ideas for perpetuating your mind
item.description:
Source: MIT Technology Review
The article explores six unconventional methods to preserve or extend human consciousness, focusing on scientific and technological approaches to maintain personal identity beyond biological limits. It begins by highlighting the mystery of self-awareness and continuity of self, prompting researchers to seek ways to sustain the mind. One idea is head transplants, inspired by 1970 experiments by neurosurgeon Robert White, who successfully reattached monkey heads but failed to restore spinal function. Italian surgeon Sergio Canavero advocates for human head transplants, citing recent pig studies where severed spinal cords were reconnected using a sealant, allowing pigs to walk again. However, critics like Grégoire Courtine dismiss these claims as implausible, arguing no technology exists to achieve such a feat. Another approach involves creating digital avatars, or 'mindclones,' as proposed by futurist Martine Rothblatt. Her vision includes uploading personal data and using AI to generate realistic digital replicas, which could eventually be granted human rights. Services like StoryFile and Synthesia now allow users to create AI-driven avatars, though they lack true self-awareness. The article also discusses Bexorg’s efforts to keep human brains alive in vats for drug testing, though these brains are metabolically active but not conscious, as they are kept under anesthesia. A separate initiative, ARPA-H’s FRONT program, aims to replace aging brain tissue with young cells to combat aging, funded with $175 million. Neuroscientist Jean Hébert envisions gradual brain replacement using lab-grown neocortical tissue, though skeptics question whether such grafts could integrate with existing brain functions. The article concludes by emphasizing the ethical and scientific uncertainties surrounding these methods, noting that while some technologies may offer partial solutions, true consciousness or identity preservation remains unproven. Researchers like Marius Wernig caution that creating functional replacement brain tissue is still in early stages, with challenges in replicating complex neural structures and ensuring compatibility with the host brain.

item.title: Meta built a huge open-weight AI model for Macs, but you'll need 1TB of RAM to run it
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Meta has released Muse Spark Open, an open-weight AI model optimized for Apple Silicon, marking its latest effort to advance US-led open-source AI development. The 800-billion-parameter model requires 1TB of RAM to run locally and is designed for Apple’s M5 Ultra-equipped Mac Studio computers. Meta claims it is "the most capable US open-weight model to date," with benchmarks suggesting it outperforms two leading Chinese models, GLM 5.3 and Kimi K3, in agentic tasks and visual reasoning. The model leverages Apple’s unified memory architecture, allowing two M5 Ultra Mac Studios to function as a single supercomputer with terabyte-level memory. A single Mac Studio with 512GB RAM or four 256GB M5 Ultra machines can host the model, though the latter setup costs approximately $38,000. Apple has not yet announced pricing or a release date for the 512GB Mac Studio, which will be available "in late October." While the high cost makes Muse Spark Open inaccessible for typical developers, larger organizations may find the investment worthwhile if the model’s performance aligns with Meta’s claims. The model is now available for download on Hugging Face. Mark Zuckerberg highlighted the collaboration with Apple and the model’s compatibility with new Mac Studios, emphasizing the potential of Apple’s hardware for running large-scale AI workloads. The release underscores Meta’s focus on open-source AI amid its stance against Chinese leadership in the field.

item.title: Steam can now show game achievements in separate ‘sets’
item.description:
Source: The Verge
Valve has introduced a new feature for Steam achievements called 'achievement sets,' allowing developers to organize achievements from a base game and its downloadable content (DLC) into separate groups. This update enables developers to create distinct progress bars for each set, making it easier for players to track their progress and identify related achievements. Players can still unlock achievements by playing the game as usual, but after completing the game, Steam will display achievements grouped into developer-created sets. Each set includes its own progress bar, and completing a set grants a 'set complete' trophy visible on the player's profile. The feature also supports seasonal achievement sets, which developers can archive, offering opportunities for time-limited content like season-based or holiday achievements. Valve highlights that this flexibility allows for creative ways to engage players, such as adding temporary achievements tied to specific events. Several games already support achievement sets, though specific titles are not listed. The updated Steam Achievements page now provides a summary of overall progress, individual set progress, and detailed achievement information. The new features are available in the latest Steam client beta, with no immediate release date specified. The change aims to enhance user experience by streamlining achievement tracking and discovery without altering the core gameplay mechanics for unlocking achievements.

item.title: E Ink's new Kaleido 4 could inch us closer to the perfect color e-reader
item.description:
Source: Engadget
E Ink has unveiled its latest color e-paper technology, the Kaleido 4, which promises significant improvements over previous versions. The new display technology aims to enhance color reproduction and refresh rates, addressing long-standing limitations of e-paper screens. According to E Ink, Kaleido 4 doubles the color gamut volume, enabling the display of over 40,000 colors, while also improving white reflectance and contrast. The refresh rate has been upgraded to support video content at 18 frames per second, a notable advancement for e-paper, though still slower than OLED screens in smartphones. These improvements could benefit future e-readers and writing tablets, as E Ink’s displays are used by major brands like Amazon, Kobo, and Boox. The Kaleido 4’s enhanced performance may allow for more accurate color images without sacrificing the clarity of black-and-white text, a drawback of earlier Kaleido 3 displays. E Ink attributes the refresh rate improvements to an oxide backplate added to the display stack, a modification similar to one Amazon implemented in its Kindle Colorsoft devices. However, the practical impact of these changes remains to be seen, as Kaleido 4 is currently only available in Hanvon Technology’s M10 C II e-paper tablet, which is exclusive to the Chinese market. The device features a redesigned front light, micro-etched glass for a paper-like writing experience, and a Kaleido 4 screen. While the technology is still in early adoption, E Ink’s advancements could bring e-readers closer to achieving the ideal balance of color accuracy and text readability.

item.title: Beta no more: Nothing OS 5 (Android 17) is rolling out for the Phone 3
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Nothing has officially launched its Android 17 (OS 5.0) update for the Phone 3, marking the end of its beta testing phase. The General Release brings significant changes, including deeper customization options, enhanced Essential AI tools, a dedicated Glyph Interface app, and a new typeface called Geist. The update is being rolled out in a staggered manner, with some users receiving it immediately while others may experience delays. Nothing advises users to check for updates via Settings > System > System Update. The Geist typeface is described as cleaner and easier to scan, replacing previous UI elements across the status bar, camera interface, Settings, and Gallery. The Glyph Interface app consolidates all features and sounds into a single location. Essential AI tools have been upgraded, with improvements to real-time transcriptions and Smart Collections, which automatically organize content. Additional updates include lock screen enhancements and personalized settings. The Phone 3 was the first device to enter the Android 17 Open Beta in late August and now the first to exit it. Other devices, including the Phone 4a, Phone 4a Pro, and Phone 3a series, remain in their respective Open Beta programs, with potential General Releases expected later in October or November. Nothing’s roadmap highlights ongoing development for these models, though no specific timelines were provided. Users are encouraged to remain patient as the update rollout continues across regions.

item.title: Withings now charges $100 per year to sync your data to other apps
item.description:
Source: The Verge
Withings has announced it will charge $100 annually for syncing health data from its smartwatches and scales to third-party apps like Apple Health or Google Health. The change affects new users creating accounts after October 12, 2026, who will need a Withings Plus subscription to access automatic data synchronization. The subscription costs $9.95 per month or $99.50 per year, with a free one-month trial that includes syncing capabilities. Once the trial expires, syncing will pause but data already stored in third-party apps will not be deleted. Existing users who created accounts on or before October 12, 2026, will retain free access to automatic syncing, regardless of whether they purchase new devices. The feature is tied to the user’s account rather than individual devices, meaning existing users can continue syncing without a subscription even if they add new hardware. The policy shift was confirmed through discussions on Withings’ support forums and official comments from a support team member. Users who subscribe will have their data automatically synced to third-party apps, while those without subscriptions will need to manually transfer data or use alternative methods. The change marks a shift in Withings’ approach to data access, prioritizing paid subscriptions for ongoing synchronization services.

item.title: How to add a second user profile to a Googlebook
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek
The article explains how to add a second user profile to a Googlebook, enabling sharing with adults, children, or guests while maintaining privacy and customization. To set up a new user profile, users must first log out of their current account via the lock screen by pressing the power button or using the battery icon in the status bar. Once logged out, the 'New user' or 'Add user' button on the login screen initiates the process. GooglebookOS will prompt for a Google sign-in, though skipping this step limits access to features requiring a Google account, such as the Play Store or Gemini. Profiles can be accessed later by signing out through the lock screen or Quick Settings. For users who disabled the 'Add user' option, the alternative is to navigate to the 'Users' section in settings under the 'System' tab, where they can add a user and assign admin privileges. Setting up a child’s account involves selecting the 'For my child' option during setup, requiring both parent and child Google accounts for parental controls, which can be managed via the Family Link app. Guest profiles, enabled by default, allow temporary access without a Google account, but they lack features like persistent storage or Gemini. To exit Guest mode, users must click the notification icon and select 'Exit Guest mode' instead of using the power button. Admin users can manage profiles, settings, and app updates, while standard users have limited control. The article emphasizes securing each profile with passwords or PINs and notes differences in parental controls between Chromebooks and Googlebooks. Overall, the feature simplifies sharing a Googlebook while preserving individual settings, especially useful with external monitors for multi-user use.

item.title: Neutron's first launch slips again amid trouble with carbon composites
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica
Rocket Lab announced Wednesday that its Neutron launch vehicle will not fly until 2027 due to manufacturing issues with the rocket’s carbon composite structures. The delay confirms widespread industry knowledge of the company’s struggles, as an August update had already hinted at potential delays beyond the end of 2024. The primary problem lies in the production of the rocket’s reusable first stage, which uses carbon composites for their lightweight, high-strength, and corrosion-resistant properties. However, aerospace-grade carbon composites are notoriously difficult to manufacture compared to metallic components. Rocket Lab’s founder and CEO, Peter Beck, attributed the delay to a defect in the manufacturing process of the propellant domes at the ends of the first stage’s fuel tanks. Engineers discovered voids, or air pockets, between layers of carbon fiber in these domes. The manufacturing process involves layering carbon fiber in a mold and curing it through heat, but large structures like the Neutron’s domes pose challenges. These components cannot fit into autoclaves—high-pressure thermal curing chambers commonly used in aerospace factories—making the process more complex. Beck stated in a video that the issue caused delays in production and required further investigation. The problem highlights the difficulties of scaling carbon composite manufacturing for large aerospace applications, as the voids compromise structural integrity. Rocket Lab’s original timeline aimed to have the first Neutron rocket ready for launch at Wallops Island, Virginia, by the end of 2024, but the defect has pushed this goal to 2027. The delay underscores the technical hurdles in producing reliable, reusable carbon composite components for rocketry, a challenge that has plagued the project since its inception.

item.title: Denis Villeneuve Sees His James Bond Movie as a ‘Powerful Rocket’ Separating Him From ‘Dune’
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo
Denis Villeneuve, director of the Dune trilogy, is transitioning from his sci-fi epic to a new high-profile project: the first James Bond film of the Amazon MGM era. After completing his Dune series, which includes the third installment set for December 18, Villeneuve described the shift as ideal, calling the Bond opportunity a 'powerful rocket' to move him away from Arrakis. In an interview with Empire, he expressed relief at breaking away from the Dune series, stating, 'I’m tired of it,' and emphasized his intention to approach the Bond material with 'severe' creativity, avoiding complacency. While the Dune films are interconnected, Villeneuve highlighted that Dune: Part Three will differ significantly from its predecessors. He noted the film will have the same 'DNA' as the series but will feature an older Paul Atreides (Timothée Chalamet) navigating a transformed world, where his actions have altered the characters' psyches and perspectives. The movie will explore Paul's struggle to escape the violence he has unleashed. The film's cast includes Zendaya, Jason Momoa, Florence Pugh, Rebecca Ferguson, Isaach de Bankolé, Charlotte Rampling, Robert Pattinson, Anya Taylor-Joy, Josh Brolin, and Javier Bardem. Villeneuve’s Bond project, which will feature an unannounced new 007 actor, marks a fresh chapter for the director after his decade-long commitment to the Dune saga.

item.title: Public Resistance Puts US Prediction Markets Under Pressure
item.description:
Source: ReadWrite
A Reuters/Ipsos poll reveals significant public resistance to prediction markets in the U.S., with six in 10 Americans opposing their use for wagering on election results. The survey of 4,506 U.S. adults conducted between September 30 and October 5 found bipartisan opposition: 69% of Democrats and 61% of Republicans expressed disapproval. Opposition extended to other government-related events, with 65% opposing bets on U.S. military actions and 63% against wagers on government policy announcements, despite low support rates of 8% and 9%, respectively. Companies like Polymarket and Kalshi, which offer markets for elections and real-world events alongside sports, claim they have safeguards against misconduct and collaborate with authorities, including reporting suspicious accounts. The poll also highlighted widespread belief that congressional members and staff should not bet on political events, with 93% of Democrats and 89% of Republicans deeming it inappropriate. In April, the Senate prohibited senators, staff, and officers from using prediction markets, while Democratic lawmakers have introduced bills to restrict the industry. Concerns include risks of insider trading, market manipulation, and national security threats. Lawmakers have called for stricter regulatory measures. Views on sports betting were more divided, with 43% opposing and 29% supporting prediction-market sports wagering. Three-quarters of respondents classified such betting as gambling, though 8% disagreed. Polymarket argued its platform primarily serves informational purposes, noting over 90% of visits are for viewing markets rather than trading. The poll underscores public sentiment amid regulatory debates, as the Trump administration seeks federal oversight while states challenge this approach. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) asserts jurisdiction over prediction markets as financial products, while state regulators argue they fall under gambling laws. Legal experts suggest the jurisdictional dispute could reach the Supreme Court, with the poll adding a political dimension to the ongoing debate over how operators like Kalshi and Polymarket can legally offer event contracts in the U.S.

item.title: This Deadly Fungus Keeps Learning How to Beat Every Drug We Throw at It
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo
A dangerous fungal strain, Candida auris, has demonstrated resistance to all four major antifungal drug classes, according to a recent study published in Scientific Reports. Researchers in Kenya identified the strain in a 28-year-old patient who developed a hospital-acquired infection after elective surgery. Despite treatment with antibiotics for a suspected bacterial infection, the patient’s wound swab revealed C. auris, which was confirmed to be resistant to all four antifungal classes. The authors warn that this resistance highlights the growing threat of untreatable fungal infections, particularly in regions with limited access to new antifungal medications. The strain’s resistance mutations differ from those in a 2022 case of pan-resistant C. auris, suggesting it may have evolved independently. While the patient’s outcome is not detailed, the hospital was informed of the resistance to implement targeted infection control measures. C. auris, previously known as Candida auris, is a superbug that can cause severe infections in immunocompromised individuals, though many carry it asymptomatically. The strain’s ability to rapidly develop resistance to common antifungals makes it particularly alarming. Global cases have risen sharply, with 6,304 reported in the U.S. in 2024 and the fungus documented in at least 50 countries. While outbreaks can still be contained through hygiene and isolation protocols, scientists caution that repeated pan-resistance could lead to widespread, untreatable infections. Researchers emphasize the need for vaccines and alternative interventions, but the fungus’s adaptability poses a persistent risk. The study underscores that C. auris remains a rare but increasingly prevalent threat, with the potential to become a major public health crisis if resistance continues to evolve unchecked.

item.title: Southwest Airlines Updates Starlink Flight Plan, Will Upgrade Entire Fleet
item.description:
Source: PCMag
Southwest Airlines has updated its plan to equip its entire fleet with SpaceX’s Starlink broadband, marking the first major U.S. airline to complete a fleetwide rollout of the service. The Dallas-based carrier announced the change in a press release that also detailed updates to its frequent-flyer program and plans for Southwest Icon lounges. The new plan involves installing Starlink on all Boeing 737 aircraft, with the rollout expected to be completed by the fall of 2027. This move follows similar decisions by American Airlines, which opted to replace older Wi-Fi systems with Starlink across its mainline fleet. Southwest previously announced in July 2023 that it would outfit 300-plus planes with Starlink by year-end, leaving around 500 aircraft to be upgraded in a fleet of 810 Boeing 737s. The airline’s initial plan had included an unspecified alternative to Starlink for some planes, but the updated strategy now focuses entirely on Starlink. The decision highlights Starlink’s advantages over traditional geostationary orbit (GEO) services, including faster downloads, improved uploads, and lower latency due to its low-Earth-orbit (LEO) position and extensive satellite constellation. Southwest also reduced in-flight Wi-Fi costs to $0 per flight in 2023 through a partnership with T-Mobile, and the new Starlink rollout aims to further enhance connectivity. While Amazon’s Leo satellite constellation is mentioned as a potential alternative, Southwest’s announcement emphasizes its commitment to Starlink. The first Starlink-equipped jet is expected to enter service this summer, with the full rollout targeting completion by 2027. United Airlines, the first major U.S. carrier to partner with Starlink, plans to finish its rollout by year-end but will exclude its smallest regional jets. Southwest’s shift underscores the growing adoption of LEO satellite technology in aviation, driven by its superior performance compared to GEO systems.

item.title: Coinbase Lays Out How It Thinks Bitcoin Should Prepare for the Quantum Threat
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo
Coinbase has outlined its vision for protecting Bitcoin from quantum computing threats, emphasizing a flexible and staged transition strategy. The exchange highlights the growing concern that quantum computers could eventually break Bitcoin’s cryptographic security, particularly for early-held funds like Satoshi Nakamoto’s coins. Coinbase’s plan includes seven key points: separating coin storage from signature schemes to allow future upgrades, implementing a 1-of-2 key system for classical and post-quantum signatures, ensuring compatibility with multi-party computation (MPC) for institutional custody, preparing for quantum threats before cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQCs) emerge, maintaining stateless signature options, ensuring robust implementations, and providing migration paths for late adopters. The company stresses that legacy funds—held in early address types with exposed public keys—should be treated as a separate governance issue, not delaying broader upgrades. Coinbase’s quantum advisory board estimates 1.7 million BTC in the oldest vulnerable addresses and 7 million BTC overall at risk. The firm advocates for quantum-safe solutions without freezing vulnerable funds, instead focusing on making upgrades accessible to those willing to adopt them. Coinbase frames its proposal as an input for open discussion rather than a directive, contrasting with its past role in the 2015–2017 block size debate, where it supported scaling solutions like SegWit2x. The company custodies about 5% of all Bitcoin and continues purchasing BTC weekly. Developers are already working on solutions, including BIP-360, P2TRv2, and a quantum-resistant transaction tested on mainnet. Coinbase supports post-quantum signature schemes like ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, and FN-DSA, as well as SHRINCS, a hybrid stateful-stateless approach. It also highlights its participation in the Bitcoin Security Consortium, which pledged $15 million to security research. While some, like Ethereum researcher Justin Drake, argue AI could break ECDSA faster than quantum computers, Coinbase’s head of cryptography, Yehuda Lindell, dismisses this as fear-mongering, citing no evidence of AI breaking cryptographic assumptions. The article underscores the need for proactive preparation, noting that Bitcoin’s consensus upgrades and ecosystem migrations typically take years, though emergency scenarios might accelerate the process.

item.title: Taking screenshots on Googlebook OS
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek
Google has introduced a new category of premium, AI-focused laptops with the Googlebook OS, which includes a streamlined Screen Capture tool for taking screenshots and screen recordings. The article details several methods to capture screenshots on the system. To take an immediate full-screen screenshot, users can press Google + S on their keyboard. For partial screenshots, pressing Google + Ctrl + S opens the Screen Capture tool with the 'Take screenshot of selected area' option. The tool can also be accessed via the Quick Settings tile, which is reachable through the top-right corner indicators, a swipe-down gesture, or the Google + Q shortcut. Some Googlebooks, like the Lenovo Googlebook 15, have a dedicated F5 key for Screen Capture, though Ctrl + F5 serves as a universal shortcut. Screen recording requires opening the Screen Capture tool and manually selecting the Record mode. The tool allows capturing entire screens, selected areas, or single app windows. Custom keyboard shortcuts for screenshot functions can be created through the Keyboard shortcuts settings. The Viewer app enables editing screenshots with cropping, resizing, annotations, and sharing, while Google Photos offers manual backup options for device folders. Despite lacking advanced features compared to tools like Windows 11's Snipping Tool, the Screen Capture tool is praised for its simplicity and efficiency, handling both basic and recording tasks seamlessly.

item.title: Riot will sunset League of Legends Classic in January 2027
item.description:

Riot Games announced that League of Legends Classic, its throwback mode, will sunset in January 2027 following the conclusion of Season 3. The mode, launched in July 2023, aimed to let players experience older versions of the game but faced declining interest, with many players returning to the main game. To address issues like long match wait times in regions with low player numbers, Riot will implement windowed queues for Classic until its closure. The studio also plans to add more champions to the Classic roster in 2026 patches. In a blog post, Riot acknowledged that enthusiasm for the mode waned quickly, stating players "have gone back to other parts of League." Despite this, the team expressed intent to revive Classic in the future, likely as a limited-time event with adjustments based on feedback. The mode was heavily promoted, including a live match at the 2023 Mid-Season Invitational featuring ten retired pro players. While similar initiatives like Blizzard’s World of Warcraft Classic have succeeded, Riot’s approach to balancing nostalgia with the evolving game did not sustain long-term engagement. The decision to sunset Classic marks the end of its three-year run, though its potential return as an event mode leaves room for future iterations.

item.title: The Ryobi tool mistakes that leave homeowners with burnt-out batteries
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek
Ryobi's ONE+ battery system is widely used for cordless power tools, but improper care can significantly shorten their lifespan. Common mistakes include using small battery packs with heavy-duty tools, exposing batteries to extreme temperatures, and allowing them to fully discharge. Small 2 Ah or 4 Ah batteries are suitable for low-drain tools like drills or screwdrivers, but using them with high-draw tools such as circular saws or impact wrenches causes rapid drainage, overheating, and premature failure. Larger 6 Ah 'HP' packs or newer EDGE batteries are recommended for heavy-duty applications to reduce strain on smaller packs. Extreme heat or cold damages lithium-ion batteries, affecting performance and longevity. Ryobi advises storing batteries in climate-controlled environments between 60°F and 77°F, allowing them to cool after use, and avoiding prolonged exposure to high temperatures. Fully discharging batteries is detrimental, as it degrades lithium-ion cells regardless of application. The manufacturer recommends keeping batteries between 40–60% charge for long-term storage, such as during winter, and avoiding complete discharge. Leaving batteries on chargers indefinitely also risks damage. Proper maintenance, including rotating battery use to prevent overcharging individual cells, can extend lifespan. The article notes that following these practices can minimize replacements, with one user reporting only one battery failure after 20 years of use, despite owning multiple older tools.

item.title: Another Good Reason to Block Online Ads: They Can Deliver Spyware
item.description:
Source: PCMag
Security researchers have uncovered evidence that online ads on websites and mobile apps were exploited to deliver spyware to devices without user consent. The spyware, linked to the Israeli company Candiru, was found infecting devices at Al Jazeera, according to a report by the Toronto-based Citizen Lab. Another Israeli firm, Discover-Tech, is alleged to have facilitated the attack by selling access to its ad platform, Controlium, to spyware developers. The platform enables zero-click attacks, where ads automatically infect devices by executing malicious code without user interaction. The ad code collects user data and sends it to Discover-Tech’s servers, which then connect to infection servers to deliver payloads via JavaScript. Citizen Lab’s report notes that the spyware was delivered to at least 45 devices within Al Jazeera between 2024 and 2025, with the attack dubbed ‘AdFection.’ The report also reveals Discover-Tech’s ads were displayed on over 70,000 mobile apps and 120,000 websites between March and June 2026, appearing on platforms like Google, Yandex, and Comcast’s Beeswax. The malicious ads were shown on devices in national-security-sensitive networks globally, including defense ministries, armed forces, cyber agencies, NATO, and critical infrastructure. Citizen Lab calls this the first public confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered via targeted ads, three years after Haaretz reported Israeli firms using ads for espionage. The research highlights how ad targeting enables mass surveillance by collecting user data, device information, and creating digital fingerprints without consent, despite existing regulations. The report also notes that the spyware’s capabilities and exploitation of software vulnerabilities remain unaddressed, though a flagged Windows DLL file from a compromised Al Jazeera device was identified as malware linked to Candiru’s attack servers.

item.title: Bluesky expands its AI-powered Attie app to let anyone build websites, games, and more

These creations will reside on the AT Protocol (ATProto), the decentralized network powering Bluesky and other apps in the Atmosphere social web. The resulting content will tap into Bluesky’s 47 million user base, though engagement has declined as some users returned to X. Bluesky COO Rose Wang noted Attie’s advantage lies in its built-in distribution through the Bluesky network, avoiding standalone limitations. The company also plans to boost developer and community activity by introducing private data support for the AT Protocol, currently in alpha testing with a planned rollout by year-end. Schneider envisions a future where users engage in 'fun, small social experiences' with friends rather than global communication. The update aligns with Bluesky’s broader strategy to revitalize its network through decentralized innovation and community-driven content.

item.title: SK Hynix bargains for chip equipment exports to its China facility in return for building a factory in US
item.description:

SK Hynix’s flash memory unit, Solidigm, is seeking U.S. approval to export advanced chipmaking equipment to its Dalian, China factory as a condition for building a semiconductor plant in the United States, according to Reuters. The move comes amid ongoing U.S. restrictions on chip equipment exports to China, which were first imposed in October 2022 and tightened in 2023. In September 2025, the Trump administration revoked special export exemptions for SK Hynix, Samsung, and Intel facilities in China, but the U.S. has since granted annual licenses to both Samsung and SK Hynix to send equipment to their Chinese plants. Solidigm, which is part of SK Hynix, is also considering upstate New York as a potential site for its U.S. factory. The company aims to install additional chipmaking equipment at its existing Dalian Mod B facility, which was completed in 2023, though SK Hynix stated it is not seeking to expand capacity there. The equipment installation is reportedly being conducted under U.S. government authorization. The U.S. government has been encouraging foreign chipmakers to build facilities domestically, with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick recently urging Samsung and SK Hynix to establish plants in the country. Solidigm is preparing for a 2027 IPO that could raise $10 billion and value the company at up to $100 billion. NAND flash chips, which Solidigm produces, are critical for solid-state storage drives used in laptops, smartphones, and AI data centers. TrendForce forecasts a 15% to 20% increase in NAND prices for the fourth quarter due to heightened demand from AI data centers, which has driven up costs for components like high-speed RAM and SSDs. The U.S. restrictions on China’s chip industry have created a complex regulatory environment, with SK Hynix balancing compliance with its global manufacturing strategy.

item.title: Singer or clanker? YouTube Music will tell you with new gen AI labeling.

YouTube Music is introducing new labels to identify AI-generated music, addressing user concerns about transparency. The rollout of the AI label marks an effort to balance innovation with consumer awareness, ensuring users can make informed choices about the music they stream.

item.title: Openreach self-install FTTP modem trial is reportedly going ahead

Openreach, part of BT, is reportedly preparing a trial to allow UK fibre broadband customers to install their own Optical Network Terminal (ONT) modems instead of having engineers perform the task. The trial, described as a "proof-of-concept," would enable customers upgrading their fibre service to replace their existing modem with a newer model, reducing setup costs compared to a full fibre installation. The trial is expected to last three months and begin before the end of 2026, involving approximately 200 participants upgrading from older Nokia ONTs with 1Gbps or slower speeds to faster multi-gig modems. The ONT, which converts optical fibre signals to electrical ones for home routers, would be delivered to customers, who would then install it themselves. However, the trial aims to address potential challenges in DIY installation. Critics note that improper installation, such as leaving the modem loose on the floor or failing to secure it properly, could lead to dust or debris entering critical ports, degrading connection quality. Another issue is insufficient fibre cable slack, which might prevent the new ONT’s port from reaching if its position differs from the old unit. Customers might attempt to force the cable or bend it excessively, risking damage. The trial will assess whether customers can handle these tasks without professional help, with solutions like wall-mounted brackets suggested to simplify future replacements. The initiative highlights the complexities of DIY fibre upgrades, balancing cost savings with technical risks.

While not the best in ANC, the headphones deliver excellent comfort, portability, and value, making them a strong choice for users prioritizing affordability and practical performance over cutting-edge noise cancellation.

item.title: Rewilding could help vulnerable islands keep pace with rising seas
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica
Coral-fringed tropical atolls, which are among the most vulnerable landforms to global warming, may have a natural defense mechanism: healthy ecosystems that can help them adapt to rising seas. A study led by marine ecologist Nick Graham of Lancaster University, published in Science Advances, analyzed 28 atoll islands across the Pacific and Indian oceans, revealing that restoring native ecosystems can reinforce their resilience against sea-level rise. The research highlights how seabirds play a critical role by transporting nutrients from the open ocean to atolls via guano, which nourishes land plants, marine life, and coral growth. This nutrient cycle supports reef-building processes, as parrotfish and other reef feeders convert dead coral into sand, maintaining beaches. Native vegetation with deep root systems also stabilizes sediments, preventing erosion. Graham emphasized that eradicating invasive species like rats and replacing monoculture coconut plantations with native forests and shrubs could give atolls a 'fighting chance' to keep pace with projected sea-level rise of up to 2°C (3.6°F) by the end of the century. The study underscores the broader potential of nature-based solutions to mitigate climate impacts, such as wetlands and forests reducing flood and fire risks while also sequestering carbon. By restoring the interconnected systems of seabirds, native vegetation, and reef ecosystems, the research suggests a virtuous cycle emerges, enhancing the islands' ability to sustain themselves amid environmental stress. The findings reinforce the importance of rewilding as a strategy to buffer against climate change, demonstrating how ecological restoration can support both natural resilience and human communities reliant on these fragile islands.

item.title: Microplastics in water aren’t inert and make damaging chemicals on their own
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica
Microplastics in water are not chemically inert and can generate harmful reactive oxygen species (ROS), according to a new study led by Wei Min, a chemist at Columbia University. The research, published in *Nature*, challenges the long-held assumption that plastics remain chemically stable once broken down. While plastics are widely used for their inertness, they degrade into microplastics that enter drinking water, human blood, and even the brain, raising concerns about their health impacts. Min’s team explored whether microplastics could produce ROS, which are known to damage proteins, lipids, DNA, and contribute to oxidative stress linked to disease. In experiments, polystyrene microplastics were stirred into water containing methyl orange, a dye that ROS break down. Over 10 days, the solution lost nearly 90% of its color, indicating ROS activity. This reaction did not occur in ethanol or other solvents, suggesting water is essential for the chemical process. The study implies microplastics may act as reactive surfaces, generating ROS that could harm biological systems. While the direct link between microplastics and human disease remains under investigation, the findings highlight the potential for microplastics to contribute to oxidative stress, a factor in various health conditions. Min noted that the boundary between water and plastic might trigger these reactions, opening new avenues for understanding microplastic toxicity. The research underscores the need for further studies to assess the long-term health risks of microplastics in the environment and human bodies.

item.title: Meta launches an open-weight AI model that runs on Macs
item.description:

Meta has launched Muse Spark Open, an open-weight AI model it claims is the "most capable" in the United States. Designed to run on Apple Macs, the model leverages 816 billion parameters and a 1 million token context window, according to evaluation results released by the company. However, running the model requires significant hardware resources, with a minimum of 1 terabyte of RAM, making it suitable primarily for high-end systems like the Mac Studio equipped with the M5 Ultra chip. Meta paired the model with its AI coding terminal, Muse Code, and demonstrated its capabilities through tasks such as coding fixes for a Mastodon client, which included "bug fixes, new features, [and] full build." The model was also used to review and crop footage in DaVinci Resolve, a high-end video editing software. Open-weight models, like Muse Spark Open, are highlighted for their cost-efficiency, transparency, and flexibility compared to closed-source alternatives. Meta is making the model available through multiple API platforms. The release underscores the growing trend of open-weight AI models offering industry advantages by enabling greater customization and reducing dependency on proprietary systems. While the model's local operation on Macs represents a notable technical achievement, its resource demands may limit accessibility for standard users, emphasizing the need for specialized hardware to harness its full potential.

item.title: Google makes it easier to find apps and listen to YouTube in your car
item.description:

Google is enhancing the in-car experience for vehicles with its built-in system by introducing a redesigned Play Store, new apps, and improved YouTube playback features. The updated Play Store aims to simplify app discovery with a more organized interface, featuring curated collections, new releases, and highlighted apps tailored to whether the vehicle is parked or in motion. The redesign also adapts to the size and orientation of each car’s infotainment screen, with one-tap downloads to streamline app installation. Additional apps like STARZ, Firefox, Ludo King, and JioHotstar are set to launch, expanding entertainment and productivity options during stops or waiting periods. YouTube receives a significant update, automatically switching to audio-only playback when drivers shift into drive, allowing videos to continue without distracting visuals. This feature requires a YouTube Premium subscription and is specific to cars with Google built-in, distinct from Android Auto, which does not currently support the same background playback functionality. The changes will be automatically rolled out to eligible vehicles over the next few weeks, improving convenience for drivers and passengers by making charging stops and waiting times more productive. Google emphasized that these updates aim to reduce the hassle of finding apps and enhance the overall entertainment experience while driving, without requiring user intervention for installation or setup.

item.title: Microsoft boasts that Windows 11 now runs much faster and more responsively
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News
Microsoft has announced that Windows 11 now runs up to 20% more responsively, based on benchmarking of typical interface workloads such as search, right-click menus, Settings, the Start menu, File Explorer, and the Snipping Tool. These performance improvements are part of the latest October update, tested in the September preview, and are compared to the OS as it existed at the start of 2026. The enhancements focus on optimizing system resource usage, particularly RAM, with significant benefits for PCs with 8GB of memory. Windows can now retain up to 2GB more active data in memory instead of offloading it to slower storage, helping maintain responsiveness when opening multiple apps or browser tabs. Background RAM usage has also been reduced, with widgets loading only when opened, cutting background workload by 200MB on 8GB or lower systems. Additionally, Microsoft highlighted improvements in memory management and efficiency, which it claims make a meaningful difference on lower-memory devices. The company also introduced a redesigned Photos app, rebuilt using WinUI 3, which launches 25% faster than before. The app features reorganized menus, tools like repair (for removing unwanted objects) and relight (for adjusting lighting), and a cleaner interface. The Photo viewer now opens photos up to 30% faster on average, with faster launch times and streamlined design. A new Gallery feature integrates photos from the PC and cloud services like OneDrive and Apple iCloud, offering natural-language search capabilities for queries like 'pictures of my dog on the beach.' Microsoft emphasized faster launch times, more responsive scrolling, and improved RAM efficiency in these updates. While the 20% responsiveness figure is described as vague, the company claims measurable gains across tested scenarios. The article notes that these changes align with Microsoft's ongoing efforts to optimize memory usage, though it raises questions about why such optimizations were delayed. Overall, the updates represent continued progress toward improving Windows 11's performance, with further tuning expected before the end of 2026.

item.title: The Google Fitbit Edge gives you a week of battery life and a screen you can use
item.description:

Google has launched the Fitbit Edge, a new fitness tracker featuring a touchscreen, advanced health monitoring, and a week-long battery life. The subscription is free for three months for new buyers. The Edge’s battery lasts up to seven days, with five minutes of charging providing a full day of use. It is water-resistant up to 50 meters and compatible with Android and iOS 16.4+ devices through the Google Health app. Available in Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon finishes, the device also features a Stephen Curry Special Edition priced at $220, developed in collaboration with the NBA player. While the Edge lacks NFC for contactless payments and has no microphone or speaker, it remains a viable option for those prioritizing health tracking and battery longevity over smartwatch features. The Fitbit Edge aims to address common frustrations with wearables by offering repairability and extended usability.

item.title: Josh Hutcherson Is Gonna Be Mister Miracle

item.title: Google, Flo Health partner to elevate women's overall well-being with Fitbit Edge
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central
Google and Flo Health have announced a multi-year partnership to enhance health features for women through the Fitbit Edge and Pixel Watch. The collaboration aims to provide personalized insights and support for women’s health, focusing on under-addressed topics like perimenopause, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), pregnancy, and postpartum recovery. Flo Health, a platform used by over 80 million women monthly, will integrate its data and algorithms into Google Health to offer tailored guidance based on sleep, cycle health, and recovery metrics. Users will be able to sync Flo Health data with Google Health starting in early 2027, ensuring privacy and data security. The Fitbit Edge, launched alongside the partnership, starts at $180 and includes advanced features such as a touchscreen, GPS, heart rate monitoring, ECG, blood oxygen tracking, and a replaceable battery for extended longevity. It also supports the Gemini-powered AI Health Coach for subscribers. Google emphasized its commitment to creating a comprehensive health experience that adapts to women’s biological and lifestyle needs, leveraging Flo Health’s expertise to improve well-being across devices like the Fitbit Edge and Pixel Watch 5. The partnership underscores Google’s focus on addressing gaps in women’s health through technology and data-driven insights.

item.title: Targeted ads delivered 0-click exploits to install mercenary malware
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica
Researchers from the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab have uncovered a sophisticated cyberattack campaign called AdFection, in which mercenary hackers used zero-click exploits embedded in targeted ads to install malware on devices without requiring any user interaction. The attack, confirmed to have infected 45 devices at international media organization Al Jazeera in 2024 and 2025, works by delivering malware through ads that trigger when users simply load a website or open an app, making it invisible to standard users. The malware, described as highly pernicious, can only be detected through specialized forensic tools. Citizen Lab warned that the attack represents a new threat vector, emphasizing that news organizations and their staff may be actively targeted, with risks extending to states and civil society. The campaign leverages Discover-Tech, an Israeli company that markets itself as a legitimate advertising firm but operates as a broker for mercenary spyware groups. Discover-Tech facilitates the distribution of ads by connecting advertisers with publishers and app developers, acting as a bridge between ad vendors and the spyware ecosystem. Advertisers pay to target specific demographics using user data such as mobile IDs, location, IP addresses, and other identifiers. Citizen Lab obtained over 4 billion bidding records from Discover-Tech, revealing that its ads were displayed across more than 70,000 mobile apps and 120,000 websites between March and June 2026. The report highlights the scale of the threat, as the company’s operations enable widespread distribution of malicious ads, raising concerns about privacy and security for users globally. Researchers stressed that the incident underscores the urgent need for heightened awareness and protective measures against such covert cyberattacks targeting both individuals and institutions.

item.title: My go-to network troubleshooting tool costs less than lunch and has no settings
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek
The article introduces a five-port unmanaged gigabit switch as a reliable, low-cost tool for network troubleshooting. Priced around the cost of a lunch, the switch has no settings, app, or web interface, making it simple and consistent for diagnosing issues. It emphasizes that cables can fail internally despite appearing intact, and the switch helps identify damaged cables by testing connectivity via LED indicators. A working cable will light up, flickering suggests damage, and no light means the cable is dead. If a cable passes the test but still fails with a PC, the problem may lie with the network adapter, driver, or motherboard jack. Testing with a laptop or USB-to-Ethernet adapter can isolate the issue. The switch also helps diagnose faulty router ports by plugging it into a known-working port and checking if the problem persists. For testing device communication, the switch can create a small isolated LAN with static IP addresses, allowing pings and file transfers to verify hardware functionality. Hidden wall cables can be tested by connecting the switch to the wall jack, revealing issues within the cable run. The switch’s reliability stems from its lack of configurable settings, ensuring trustworthy results. The article recommends the NETGEAR 8-Port Gigabit Ethernet Unmanaged Switch (GS308) as a dependable, affordable option for such tasks.

item.title: Investigation Finds Hundreds of ‘Injuries and Dangerous Malfunctions’ at Six Flags Before Lethal Goliath Accident
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo
A fatal accident at Six Flags Over Georgia, where 42-year-old Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem fell to his death after being ejected from the Goliath roller coaster, has reignited scrutiny of the company’s safety practices. The incident, which also injured several riders, follows a CNN investigation revealing hundreds of injuries and dangerous malfunctions at Six Flags parks over the past five years. The company temporarily closed at least 10 rides across its parks, exacerbating concerns about its safety record and contributing to an 80% drop in its stock price since a 2024 merger with Cedar Fair. CNN’s analysis of maintenance and safety records from over a dozen parks in three states highlighted recurring issues, including train derailments, faulty restraint bars, and guest injuries such as dislocated joints and concussions. In California, Six Flags reported nearly 300 accidents since 2021 under state reporting laws requiring medical service beyond basic first aid. New Jersey’s Six Flags Great Adventure faced a 2024 derailment, seven log ride evacuations, and a head injury incident, while its El Toro coaster was shut down for over a year after a 2022 incident injured over a dozen riders. Texas parks saw frequent reports of patrons being thrown from water park rides and other injuries. Six Flags’ statement acknowledged the severity of incidents but noted varying state regulations and incomplete data, cautioning against broad conclusions. The Georgia tragedy follows another CNN investigation into Six Flags Magic Mountain’s X2 coaster, which was permanently shut down after two riders required brain surgery in July 2024 and over 100 others reported brain injuries. Two investor lawsuits allege the company neglected routine maintenance for years. Regulatory oversight remains fragmented, as the federal Consumer Product Safety Commission lost jurisdiction over theme parks in 1981, leaving states to set their own standards. While the International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions estimates a 1 in 15.5 million risk of serious injury, data is incomplete and voluntary, according to The Regulatory Review. The incident underscores ongoing safety concerns and regulatory gaps in the industry.

item.title: NY congressman to introduce bill protecting video game ownership
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Representative Ritchie Torres (D-NY) plans to introduce the Power to the Players Act, a bill aimed at ensuring consumers can retain ownership and play video games they’ve purchased. The legislation would direct the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to regulate digital game sales, preventing companies from revoking access to games after purchase. Torres cited NBA 2K25 as a key example, noting the game was released in 2024 for $70 but will be removed from digital storefronts on October 30, 2025, with its online servers shut down in December. This effectively leaves players without access to the game they paid for. The bill would require companies to grant permanent ownership of games rather than licensing them and mandate offline play options if online servers are discontinued. In an interview with Kotaku, Torres called the measure a 'restoration to the historical norm' before digital sales dominated, and suggested it could inspire similar protections for digitally purchased books, movies, and music. However, the bill faces significant challenges. It could stall in Congress, mirroring a failed California state bill from June 2025. Legal hurdles also loom, as the 2024 Supreme Court decision overturning Chevron deference has weakened federal agencies’ regulatory authority. Under this ruling, the FTC’s attempts to enforce the law could be blocked by courts, similar to how its noncompete clause ban was struck down. Engadget has requested a draft of the bill and comments from Torres on the FTC’s potential legal limitations, with updates pending.

item.title: Sony Created a Gold-Plated Walkman That Costs Nearly $6,000
